chunks: As for what Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn Yaḥyā narrated from his father, from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from Ḥammād ibn ʿUthmān, from ʿUbayd Allāh al-Ḥalabī, from Abū ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام, who said:

If you perform some prayer during travel at other than its time, then it does not harm. The correct understanding of this report is that this refers to one who prays outside the time, meaning after the time has passed, so it does not harm him because he is making it up. But before the entry of the time, it is not permissible, whether he is a traveler or resident.

key_terms.السَّفَرِ: travel; the state of being a traveler
key_terms.خُرُوجِ الْوَقْتِ: the expiry of the prayer time
key_terms.دُخُولِ الْوَقْتِ: the beginning or entry of the prayer time
key_terms.قَاضِيًا: performing the prayer as a make-up prayer

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to perform salat (prayer) before or after its prescribed time while traveling?
ai.summary: This report addresses the ruling of performing salat (prayer) outside its appointed time, especially in travel. It explains that praying after the time has exited may be valid as qaḍāʾ, but praying before the time begins is not permissible for either a traveler or a resident.
